intro: Nurse practitioners make clinical decisions, educate patients and lead care, so their closest matches are in teaching, counseling and research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary, with a 74% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $107,310, which is 19% less than the $132,300 nurse practitioners earn.
why_it_works: Your days combine assessing patients, prescribing and explaining care plans to patients who may be anxious or confused. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and judgment and social perceptiveness at 4. Teaching, genetic counseling and clinical research use the same depth. Because your pay is already high, only 3 matches pay more. The gaps are programming and instructing groups.
tips: Teach part time in a nursing program before leaving practice; it tests whether academic work suits you.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, which is 11% more, and use your precision with doses and safety.
Clinical research coordination keeps you close to patients with a median of $167,220 for its broader group.

faq.q: What jobs can former nurse practitioners do?
faq.a: The closest matches are postsecondary health specialties teachers (74%), Genetic Counselors (73%) and clinical research coordinators (68%), based on O*NET 31.0. Health Informatics Specialists are also 67% matched, with a median of $105,850 for their broader group, and suit practitioners who like data and systems.

faq.q: Which careers for nurse practitioners pay more?
faq.a: Only 3 of the 25 matches pay more than $132,300. Industrial-Organizational Psychologists earn $193,950 (47% more), Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (11% more) and Political Scientists $142,080 (7% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Each needs specific training in that field.

faq.q: Do nurse practitioners need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: No for every match on this page: all 25 usually need no more education than nurse practitioners already have. A master's degree is common, held by 91% of workers in a close match, so your graduate nursing degree covers most formal requirements.

faq.q: What skills should nurse practitioners build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are programming, instructing, operations monitoring and quality control analysis. Service orientation already rates 3.88 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so teaching and data skills are the main steps outside clinical practice for most people.
